points.text: Novelty over feature hedging thin; L0 effect not separated from width.
Related work brief; misses Leask, Toy Models, SAEBench, Paulo and Belrose.
'Any L0 equally valid' framing argues against a straw man.
No competing L0 selection baselines (elbow, probing, absorption).
Citations for low-L0 harm claim need supporting quotes.
LLM 'correct L0' defined only by coarse proxy peaks; probing may favor larger L0.
'Most SAEs have too-low L0' extrapolated from one configuration.
Toy uses orthogonal features without superposition.
Toy cannot separate low-L0 mixing from width-driven hedging; width unstated.
Metric minimum lies in flat region, depends on n, lacks derivation.
One seed per L0, 500M tokens; high-L0 SAEs possibly under-trained; no variance.
n values in text differ from figure.
'Higher MSE' statement contradicts reported numbers.
Symbols n, N, k used interchangeably.
Tuning procedure not demonstrated in LLMs.
LLM evidence from one model, layer, width and proxy.
No repeated seeds or uncertainty; high-L0 SAEs may be under-trained.
Coarse L0 grid makes '200-250' estimate few points.
Toy lacks superposition and overcompleteness.
Toy uses one correlation matrix, one run, three L0 values; no recovery curve.
Toy SAE width and training hyperparameters unstated.
Metric is ungrounded heuristic; minimum ill-defined; no estimator.
Sparse probing validation weak, no error bars, may rise with L0 anyway.
Headline 'most SAEs L0 too low' runs ahead of evidence.
Generalization to JumpReLU and L1 SAEs asserted without experiment.
Typos.
Symbols n/N/k used interchangeably.
LLM evidence small relative to community-level claim.
Central evidence and procedure placed in appendix.
Notation n, N, k drifts.
Text and Figure 2 give different n values.
Eq. 3 transpose possibly inconsistent with stated shape.
Related work only four sentences.
Abstract claims ('precisely', same decoder patterns in Gemma) exceed experiments.
Typos, possible anonymization issue, missing statements.
Toy lacks superposition, heavy-tailed frequencies, varying active counts.
Assumption of a single true L0 and atomic feature set untested.
Probing measures usefulness not correctness; no downstream evaluation.
No classical model-order-selection baselines.
Automatic procedure fragile in LLMs; practitioners cannot yet set L0.
Cost and interpretability trade-off of high L0 not discussed.
Presentation and figures subpar.
Missing MDL-SAE related work.
Lacks theoretical grounding; purely empirical.
Toy assumes orthogonal, linearly separable features unlike real LLMs.
Metric needs manual hyperparameter tuning; automatic procedure hard.
LLM experiments limited to few layers.
Contribution unclear beyond showing L0 hyperparameter matters.
Unclear what the metric measures or its intended utility.
Metric requires trained SAEs, so does not reduce search cost.
No added benefit of metric over sparse probing scores.
Missing feature-splitting related work.
Missing quasi-orthogonality SAE metric work.
Novelty relative to feature hedging paper unspecified.
Not shown that heuristic picks better SAEs among SAEBench models.
Missing ICA source-number estimation literature.
Plots inconsistent: decoder projections and high-L0 not shown throughout.
Selection of n somewhat arbitrary.
Feature frequency alternative explanation for low-L0 results.

P.summary: Novelty vs feature hedging thin; L0 vs width not disentangled.
Related work thin, missing key prior work.
Probing-only LLM validation weak; usefulness not correctness.
LLM evidence narrow: one model, layer, width.
Toy lacks superposition and realistic feature statistics.
Metric ungrounded; minimum ill-defined and n-dependent.
Single seeds, no variance, possible under-training.
n values inconsistent between text and figure.
Abstract precision and pattern claims overstated.
Cost/interpretability trade-off of high L0 ignored.

Q.summary: Missing related work (MDL, splitting, quasi-orthogonality, ICA).
Metric needs manual tuning; automatic procedure hard.
No validation selecting better pretrained SAEs.
